content.title: Olde Town Arvada pavement improvements, temporary parklet removal begin May 11
content.summary: Starting May 11, 2026, the City of Arvada will conduct street pavement maintenance in the Olde Town Arvada Pedestrian Zone, which includes the removal of parklets and outdoor seating. The project aims to enhance safety and aesthetics in the area, with work expected to be completed by May 22, allowing businesses to remain open during construction. The City is coordinating with local businesses to minimize disruption and plans to introduce new murals later in the year.
content.body:
Arvada, CO – The City of Arvada will be doing regular street pavement maintenance in the Olde Town Arvada Pedestrian Zone starting Monday, May 11, 2026. The work is part of ongoing efforts by the City to keep the popular business district safe, attractive, and friendly to pedestrians.

All parklets and outdoor seating areas, fireplaces, and electric (string lights) along the streets in the Pedestrian Zone will be removed as part of the project. The Pedestrian Zone is located on Grandview Avenue between Webster Street and Olde Wadsworth, and on Olde Wadsworth between Grandview Avenue and Grant Place. All businesses will remain open during the project.

Work will include crack sealing and street sealing in the area. Crews will also need to strip the existing street murals in the Pedestrian Zone, which were installed in 2021. The City of Arvada and the Arvada Arts and Culture Commission will begin planning for new murals later in 2026. 

Work is expected to begin on May 11 with patio and parklet removal and stripping of the current murals, continuing through the week of May 16. Weather permitting, work should be completed and all outdoor elements are expected to be returned by May 22. 

The City is coordinating with the Olde Town Arvada Business Improvement District (BID) to keep the businesses in the area informed of the project. "We have been in communication with businesses already to ensure the impact of this project on the popular Olde Town district is minimal," said City of Arvada Deputy City Manager Allison Scheck. Businesses have the option to remove and store the outdoor elements themselves, or have the City store them for the duration of the construction work.

While businesses will remain open, visitors to Olde Town will notice that streets are coned and taped off and shipping containers will be placed on side streets. Pedestrians are advised to avoid the taped off areas for their safety and so as not to disrupt crews working in the area.

The timing of the work will help prevent too much disruption over the summer. "We're excited for Olde Town to be getting a face lift before we see an influx in visitors for our busy summer season," said Olde Town BID Interim Executive Director Jean Gordon. The City also recently established a designated drinking area in Olde Town, which is expected to increase visits to the Pedestrian Zone this summer.
